item.title: Can Fantasy Football Managers Trust Jonah Coleman In Week 9 And Moving Forward With Jonathan Taylor Looming?
item.description: Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) on the field prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We had another exciting fantasy football Sunday in Week 8, and it was especially exciting for Jonah Coleman owners. The rookie had his breakout game, but we've seen running backs do this in Denver in the past, then fizzle out. That leads us to one obvious question: can you trust Denver Broncos rookie running back moving forward? Jonah Coleman vs JK Dobbins In Week 8, Coleman dominated the Broncos' backfield, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps, with JK Dobbins playing on just 21%. Coleman carried the ball 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown, and caught four of his five targets for another 63 yards. Dobbins took just seven carries for 13 yards and wasn't targeted in the passing attack. It does not seem like a fading Dobbins is going to be a significant issue. That doesn't mean he won't play more than he did this week, but we are confident that Coleman will be the lead back. However, RJ Harvey could return after three more games. If Dobbins continues to see around seven carries, and Harvey cuts into Coleman's passing-down work, it could cap his upside. Nevertheless, that won't be anytime in the immediate future, with Harvey being placed on injured reserve last week. Jonathan Taylor To Denver There is also another looming threat that could be a major issue for Coleman. The Broncos are one of the teams that have been linked to a potential trade for Jonathan Taylor. The hope is that Coleman played well enough to convince the Broncos they don't need Taylor. Nevertheless, if they do end up trading for JT, he is going to be the bell-cow back in Denver. Still, there have been a handful of teams linked to Taylor, and this is far from a lock. Can You Trust Jonah Coleman? There are some potential pitfalls, but we are going to roll with the rookie. We projected him to take over the starting job in Denver around midseason, and that's exactly what's happening. It would be crazy to back off of what we've said along as we see it happening in real time. As long as they don't make a move for Taylor, which we aren't expecting, you can trust Coleman moving forward. We don't view either Dobbins or Harvey as serious threats. Although they could cut into his workload a bit at times, it will not be enough to seriously damage his fantasy viability. Notre Dame made its trip to Rome even more memorable by completing a sweep of Villanova, with the women’s team following the men’s victory with a convincing 99-75 win in the opening game of the season. Head coach Niele Ivey had plenty of reasons to celebrate, especially after watching the Fighting Irish men secure their own victory against the Wildcats the previous day. “What’s better than one win is two,” Ivey said, according to the Associated Press, referring to Notre Dame’s sweep of Villanova in Rome. Both programs also enjoyed a special experience in the Eternal City, including an audience with Pope Leo XIV, a Villanova alumnus, during the Eternal City Tip-Off festivities. On the court, Hannah Hidalgo immediately reminded everyone why she entered the season as one of the country’s top players. The senior guard delivered 32 points, eight assists, seven rebounds, and three steals, shooting 11-of-19 from the field. Her impact went beyond the box score, highlighted by an impressive sequence in which she intercepted a pass and leaped out of bounds to keep the play alive before finding a teammate. After missing her entire freshman season because of a knee injury sustained in high school, the sophomore forward erupted for 27 points and 14 rebounds, giving the Irish another major offensive contribution. Villanova received 26 points from Jasmine Bascoe, but her team struggled to keep pace with Notre Dame’s offensive firepower. For Ivey, the result was an ideal start to the campaign. item.title: Jake Paul to fight ex-kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe
item.description: Jake Paul (pictured) will fight Cedric Doumbe in a boxing bout Dec. 24 at Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai. File Photo by Steve Ferdman/UPI Nov. 2 (UPI) -- Jake Paul will take on former kickboxing world champion Cedric Doumbe in a boxing bout Dec. 24 in Dubai, Most Valuable Promotions announced Monday. Paul announced Thursday that he planned to return to boxing on Christmas Eve for the first time since he sustained a broken jaw during a loss to Anthony Joshua on Dec. 19 in Miami. Press conferences for the bout will be held Nov. 10 in Paris and Nov. 12 in Dubai. The fight will be held at Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai. "Cedric [expletive] was calling me out two years ago after knocking some dude out in nine seconds," Paul said in a news release. "Well [expletive], now you get your chance. I'm rusty, my jaw is janky and I don't have kickboxing world titles like you do. But guess what, this isn't kickboxing, mon ami. This is boxing. "Just like Usyk feasted on Rico Verhoeven, I am going to eat you for dinner in Dubai on Christmas Eve and have a Coca-Cola at the arena to celebrate. You like to talk a lot, so let's see what you have to say in person at the press conferences next week in Paris and Dubai. To the proud people of France, excuse-moi for what I am about to do, but your son has been naughty and he's going to get punished. To all the fans in Dubai and all of MENA. ... We are doing this and we are doing it big, like Dubai always does. I'm baaaaaccccccccck." Doumbe, who was born in Cameroon and raised in France, has a 75-7-1 record, with 45 knockouts, in professional kickboxing. He is 6-1, with six knockouts, in mixed martial arts. The 34-year-old beat Mohamed Fodil in his lone boxing bout in 2015. Paul (12-2 in boxing) won the first six bouts of his career. He took his first loss -- by split decision -- in 2023 to Tommy Fury. The 29-year-old went on to win his next six bouts before his loss to Joshua. "Jake Paul calls himself the 'Problem Child,' but he's never faced a problem like me," Doumbe said. "He has no idea what a Frenchman is capable of, and on Thursday, Dec. 24 in Dubai, I'm going to eat 'El Poulet' for dinner. Jake loves to talk, and so do I, but after what Joshua did to his jaw, I'm not sure how much talking he has left. "I'm going to finish the job Joshua started. Dubai is a special city to me, and on Christmas Eve, I'll be waving le Tricolore over his unconscious body. France, this one's for you."

item.title: Highest-ever! Afghanistan make historic leap, overtake Sri Lanka, England and West Indies in ODI rankings
item.description: Afghanistan have reached a historic milestone in international cricket, breaking into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time and moving ahead of former world champions Sri Lanka, England and the West Indies. The Afghans have climbed to sixth place in the latest rankings, surpassing Sri Lanka to secure their highest-ever position in the 50-over format. It marks another significant chapter in the remarkable rise of a side that made its ODI debut only in 2009 and has steadily established itself among the most competitive teams in international cricket. Their latest achievement is particularly significant given the established cricketing nations they have overtaken. Afghanistan had already moved ahead of Bangladesh, England and the West Indies in the rankings and have now gone past Sri Lanka to break into the top six. From debutants to a force in world cricket Afghanistan's rise has been built on consistent performances and landmark victories against some of the biggest names in the game. Since making their ODI debut in 2009, they have won 96 of their 191 matches, boasting an impressive win-loss ratio of 1.09. Their progress gathered momentum during the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, where they produced memorable victories over former champions Pakistan and Sri Lanka. 135456019 They carried that confidence into the shortest format, reaching the semi-finals of the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup for the first time. The campaign further underlined their growing stature, as they demonstrated their ability to compete with the world's leading sides on the biggest stage. Winning momentum fuels historic rankings rise Afghanistan's latest climb has been backed by an impressive run of results in recent months. They began their recent surge with a dominant 4-0 away series victory over Ireland before maintaining an unbeaten record in the tri-series involving Zimbabwe and Bangladesh. Their impressive form has also extended to T20Is. Afghanistan recently completed a 3-0 series whitewash against Zimbabwe, sealing the clean sweep with a convincing seven-wicket victory in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday. The Afghans will now turn their attention to the longest format, with a two-match Test series against Zimbabwe next on the schedule.

item.title: Why Joe Buck and Troy Aikman is the most painful breakup in sports media history
item.description: Credit: ESPN / Edit via Liam McGuire Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have just a few months left together at the top of the mountain in sports broadcasting. Their journey to the summit of the industry has been filled with praise from fans and respect from peers. But the path back down has been one of regret and ruination. After 25 years together on a lead NFL broadcast team, Buck and Aikman will almost certainly go their separate ways after this season following an astounding public estrangement centered around their individual contracts with ESPN. Joe Buck was signed to a new contract extension earlier this year. However, Troy Aikman was not. That led to reports of a fierce, profane argument in the Monday Night Football booth that is now the stuff of sports media legend. After years being the gold standard in sports broadcasting, the story of Joe Buck and Troy Aikman is now a brittle and bitter tale. Accusations of betrayal , leaks to the media , and hurt feelings on display have cast a long, dark shadow over what was going to be a celebratory season for Disney, ESPN, and the Monday Night Football franchise with their return to the Super Bowl rotation. If the Buck and Aikman connection does come to an end in February 2027, it will mark a a truly unfortunate demise. And barring some kind of dramatic reconciliation, it will stand as the new gold standard for sports media breakups for a number of reasons. The longevity It’s almost impossible to believe because neither Joe Buck, nor Troy Aikman look like grizzled veterans in the broadcast booth. But the pairing is believed to be the record holder for the longest-running broadcast booth in major sports media history. Buck and Aikman have worked an incomparable 25 seasons together leading NFL coverage at Fox and ESPN. (The first few years at Fox they were a trio with Cris Collinsworth.) Credit: NFL on Fox Together, they have called over 300 regular season games together on national television, 20 NFC Championship Games, five seasons of Monday Night Football , and Super Bowl LXI, presumably their last telecast together , will be their seventh Super Bowl. That will tie the record set by the legendary duo of John Madden and Pat Summerall. That tenure spanning a quarter of a century has not only surpassed Summerall and Madden as the NFL standard bearers for longevity, but plenty of other historic broadcasting combinations as well. item.title: Spalletti can see the benefit of the training retreat already
item.description: Spalletti can see the benefit of the training retreat already Luciano Spalletti is delighted that Juventus secured a victory over Napoli at the weekend, with the manager believing the team retreat before the match played an important role in preparing his players for the challenge. Following the defeat against Genoa , Spalletti decided to take decisive action by ordering his players into a retreat. The squad remained together at the club’s facility until their next match, giving the manager an opportunity to bring everyone closer and address the issues affecting the team. The decision appears to have produced the desired response, as Juventus came through a difficult encounter with a victory they might not have secured during a less settled period. Spalletti is pleased with the outcome, although he does not believe the team will need to repeat the same approach every time they want to win. Spalletti explains why the retreat helped Juventus Juventus showed greater confidence during the match, particularly after the break, when they managed to make progress and put Napoli under pressure. Although their overall performance was not exceptional, the players continued to push for a positive result and eventually got their reward. The manager believes spending time together helped his squad reconnect and rediscover the sense of unity required to move forward. He also acknowledged that his players did not always make the right decisions, but was satisfied with their willingness to keep trying. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Manager praises his players after Napoli victory Speaking via Tuttojuve , Spalletti explained why the retreat had been beneficial and praised the collective response from his players. “The retreat was useful because they’re a group of guys who love each other and needed to be close, to find something familiar. You reconnect with the group, you find yourself within a group that loves each other, and it becomes easier to take that step forward. They did it during the match, they gained ground, and in the second half they deserved to win. Admittedly, they didn’t play an extraordinary game, but they deserved the win. We didn’t always choose well, but we had shots on target. We had four shots on target, seven off, and seven shots were blocked by defenders inside the box, some of them a bit awkwardly. But we tried. They really made these steps forward, and then they were rewarded with a fantastic goal from a talented player.” Spalletti will hope the victory provides a foundation for greater consistency, allowing Juventus to build momentum without needing another retreat to restore confidence and togetherness.

item.title: Overtime goal lifts Bethlehem past Guilderland for 2nd straight Class A field hockey title
item.description: Bethlehem's Lauren Brodeur reacts in Gabby Pesca's arms after scoring the game-winning goal in overtime of the Section 2 Class A championship game on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) GLENS FALLS - The first three times the Bethlehem field hockey team went into overtime this season, things didn't go their way. The Eagles ended their bad fortune in overtime Sunday in the Section 2 Class A championship game, as Lauren Brodeur finished a penalty corner on a ball sent in by Ava Austin. Brodeur's dramatic goal secured a 1-0 win over top-seeded Guilderland, handing the No. 2 Eagles their second straight Section 2 championship. "It's just a dream come true to score a goal like that," Brodeur said, "and I did it with my best friends." Neither team got many clean looks on goal during the scoreless regulation period, setting up the dramatic overtime finish. "It was definitely a defensive battle throughout the midfield, but Guilderland is a very skilled team," said Bethlehem coach Dawn Austin. "They're fast on their feet and they're athletic, and we had to match their hard work today." "We worked really well together to keep the ball out of the circle," added senior forward Chelsea Biche, "and really just to keep it away from the goal." The Eagles also captured the 2025 Class A title with a 1-0 win over Guilderland. "I knew if I sent the ball to her, she'd be able to read the defense and feed it to whoever was open." "All of a sudden I saw it and I just hit it in," Brodeur said of finishing off the walk-off goal from the middle of the circle, as she sent it to the left of Guilderland goalie Alaina Dipierro. item.title: Do you believe Liverpool was denied a penalty against Arsenal?
item.description: Do you believe Liverpool was denied a penalty against Arsenal? Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield , ending their 14-year wait for a win at the ground. The result was an important achievement for Mikel Arteta’s side, who had struggled to secure victories there during that period. The previous time the Gunners won at Anfield was in 2012, when Arteta was still a player under Arsène Wenger. However, he had never managed to guide Arsenal to victory at the stadium until yesterday, making this result particularly significant for the Spaniard. An early goal from Kai Havertz proved decisive, with the German once again demonstrating his ability to deliver in important moments. His contribution gave Arsenal the advantage they needed to secure all three points. Liverpool dominated large periods of the contest, struck the post and created opportunities to score. However, Arsenal defended resolutely and managed to protect their lead, strengthening their position at the top of the Premier League table. Liverpool left frustrated by penalty decision Despite Arsenal’s victory, there was considerable controversy surrounding a potential penalty that Liverpool believed should have been awarded. Footage from the match appeared to show Jurrien Timber pulling Alexander Isak’s shirt as the Swedish striker attempted to reach a header inside the penalty area. Isak remained on his feet following the contact, and VAR did not intervene. The decision angered Liverpool’s players, supporters and manager, who felt their side had been denied an important opportunity to equalise. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images) Iraola questions officials over Isak incident Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola was particularly unhappy with the decision and insisted that the contact on Isak should have resulted in a penalty. Speaking after the match, he explained his frustration, as reported by the Daily Mail : ‘There are two situations and they are a little bit related. The Isak one is a clear penalty. ‘He’s gonna head the ball in front of the goal, and they grab him where everyone sees the shirt. You don’t need a lot, just to avoid Alex, because the ball just goes in front of him, and I don’t see the reason why, probably because he doesn’t dive or he doesn’t go to the floor. item.title: Jeff Passan Shuts Down Trade Rumors Surrounding Brewers' William Contreras
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers catcher William Contreras The Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series, but there are rumors that World Series MVP William Contreras could get traded this offseason. These rumors are not out of left field. He has one year left before hitting free agency, and history suggests that the Brewers would consider dealing him before he walks and they get nothing. They did so with Josh Hader, Freddy Peralta, Devin Williams and even Cy Young Award winner Corbin Burnes. Contreras is one of the best catchers in the game, and his price on the open market will surely be more than what the Brewers typically pay. However, trading him after winning the World Series seems foolish, and Jeff Passan made it clear the Brewers will not do that. "William Contreras isn't going anywhere even though he is nearing free agency," Passan wrote on Monday for ESPN . Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? The Brewers knew he was too valuable to the culture, and they did not have a replacement ready. They are in a similar boat with Contreras. However, Contreras could be a rare exception to their spending rules. Christian Yelich's contract will expire in a few years, and the Brewers will have room to pay a star player. Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt and Luis Lara are under contract for years to come, and Jesús Made is expected to sign an extension soon as well. They can certainly afford to pay Contreras if they want. Whether they do remains to be seen, but it seems like they will at least let him play out his final season before free agency. item.title: Eagles could make an OC change soon: 3 options to replace Sean Mannion
item.description: LANDOVER, Md. — The Eagles’ offense, as it has all year, struggled in the Eagles’ 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday night at Northwest Stadium. Following the game, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni was asked whether he would demote or fire offensive coordinator Sean Mannion after another poor offensive showing. Sirianni didn’t exactly defend Mannion, leaving room for interpretation that the Eagles could be considering an offensive coordinator change. “I’m not thinking about any of that stuff right now,” Sirianni said after the game. “We need to get better as a whole, and I got a lot of faith in everybody in that locker room. I got a lot of faith in the coaches in that locker room. I’ll keep it at that.” This past offseason, the Eagles hired Mannion to bring in a new scheme that they hoped would ignite a stagnant offense, but Mannion’s play-calling has not been transformational. Instead, Philadelphia’s offense has become even worse under Mannion. The Eagles managed 10 points against the Commanders, who had allowed the second-worst points-per-game average (28.7) over the first seven weeks of the season. Mannion’s offense converted only 5 of 15 third-down attempts, allowed five sacks for a loss of 35 yards and rushed for only 91 yards. Mannion’s offense was a disaster again. The Eagles entered their Week 8 matchup against the Commanders ranked near the bottom in every offensive category, which reflects poorly on Mannion. During Mannion’s first season, circumstances have not been easy: the Eagles lost starting quarterback Jalen Hurts to a season-ending injury and right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement, among other problems. But Mannion has struggled to elevate lesser talent with a creative scheme. Mannion’s players have struggled to execute his concepts, which suggests his coaching points are not resonating. Growing pains were expected, but it is past that point now. Mannion is not a good play-caller. Here are three in-house candidates who could replace Mannion: Pass game coordinator Josh Grizzard Grizzard is the most obvious choice to supplant Mannion as the Eagles’ play-caller. He interviewed for the Eagles’ offensive coordinator job this offseason before the team hired Mannion. Grizzard made a good impression during his interviews, which helped him earn a role on the offensive staff. He was the Buccaneers’ offensive coordinator last season, but Tampa Bay fired him after the offense collapsed late in the season. The Buccaneers had some good moments under Grizzard, including scoring 29, 38 and 30 points in three wins early in the 2025 season. Grizzard could be a better offensive coordinator the next time around. Could that opportunity come soon with the Eagles? He might provide the team with more stability than Mannion. item.title: Stokell in 'voluntary' ban after medication error
item.description: Rebecca Stokell has played 109 times for Ireland [Getty Images] Ireland cricketer Rebecca Stokell said she will "fully accept" responsibility for an inadvertent breach of reporting requirements regarding the use of prescription medication and has begun a "voluntary suspension". The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed the 26-year-old was drug tested and "returned an adverse finding for a specified substance" after her side's defeat by Sri Lanka at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in June. Although the substance was not performance-enhancing, Stokell has acknowledged she did not adhere to reporting requirements over the use of prescription medication and has started a voluntary period of suspension while waiting for the outcome of an ICC investigation. "I fully accept my mistake and have voluntarily entered into a period of suspension ahead of the findings being returned," said Stokell in a statement. "While this was not performance-related in any way, I understand that I am responsible for following the anti-doping guidelines and I hope that I can be back playing for Ireland as soon as possible." Graeme West, the director of high performance at Cricket Ireland, added: "While we feel very sorry for Rebecca and have provided the level of support appropriate in these circumstances, this incident does serve as a reminder to all our international players that the anti-doping rules are in place to protect both the sport and the athletes themselves. "All players must adhere to the standards and responsibilities expected, and we will continue to educate our players regularly on these matters and why they are important." Stokell made her international debut in 2017 and has featured 109 times for Ireland across all formats.

item.title: Rice: Liverpool win boosts Arsenal’s hopes of title defence
item.description: Arsenal's Declan Rice celebrates after the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield. (is associated with: «Rice: Liverpool win boosts Arsenal’s hopes of title defence») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice said ending a 14-year winless Premier League run at Anfield strengthened confidence they can retain their title but stressed the players will not get carried away. The 1-0 victory not only ended a barren spell stretching back to 2012 but also took Mikel Arteta – who played in the last team to win at Liverpool in the league – back to the top of the table, three points ahead of Manchester City and nine ahead of their fifth-placed opponents. Asked whether the victory had bolstered belief of being able to go back-to-back, Rice said: “Yeah, I think any team who has won here in the past has never had it easy. “It’s always going to be tough coming to Anfield so we had to dig in, we had to give it everything because they throw so many attacks at you. “We had to be resilient and strong. It’s just drilled into us what this manager has built at this club and the togetherness of the lads – you don’t get that performance without the lads being all together. “The way the manager has everything under control, the way everyone works towards everything he wants is not like anything I’ve ever seen before, so credit to us for what we have been doing for the last few years. “It’s a massive thing to deliver again this year and keep pushing. We’ve set those demands on ourselves and it’s up to us to keep delivering that and this adds towards that. “I’ve learned in this league November means nothing. You just have to win as much as you can and in February or March, if you are there or thereabouts, you are in with a chance. “Look at Liverpool. They have secretly gone under the radar, their attack is incredible, the defence is really good. Man City have started really strong, Chelsea are there or thereabouts so just keep winning and take each game as it comes and see where it takes us.” Such was Arsenal’s organization and commitment they became the first team to prevent Liverpool having a shot on target in a Premier League match at Anfield since records began in 2003. While the performance was not particularly pretty, it proved effective. “What I’ve learned in this league is that every game is different, no game is plain sailing, it is always going to be tough,” Rice added. “Looking back at that Forest game (a 1-0 win last month), it wasn’t the best performance but we ground it out and we won and there’s going to be more of that this season. “But results like this just make it that extra bit special, so we are delighted.”

item.title: Brittany Mahomes Is Right: That Ref Call Was A Joke
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Brittany Mahomes called out the officials after a bad call cost the Kansas City Chiefs their win on Sunday. She could not believe how bad that call was at the end of the game. The New York Post reported she posted this message on her Instagram Stories after the 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. She is right to be angry because the rules were not followed. The Chiefs had the ball on the 2-yard line with seconds left. A false start penalty pushed them back to the 7-yard line. Patrick Mahomes was sacked on the next play to end the game. Reports say the flag was called for the slightest movement. The rulebook does not allow for such a small move to kill a score in the final seconds. The Penalty That Changed Everything The call on Jaylon Moore was the reason the game ended in a loss. The team had over 100 yards in penalties during the contest. Coach Andy Reid said the guys battled like crazy but too many penalties hurt them. He observed that the poor moments placed the team in a poor situation right through the finish. Reid called the flag one man’s opinion in that moment. He did not see a false start himself. The penalty made it fourth-and-goal from the 7-yard line. The Chiefs folded in the fourth quarter again. This pattern of mistakes is what fans cannot ignore. A Pattern Of Bad Calls This is not the first time replay has made a mistake this season. The Big 12 admitted that a replay call was incorrect in a game between BYU and Arizona State. The league said replay was incorrect in awarding a score. According to the rule, possession goes to the recovering team at the recovery spot, and any advance is canceled. The BYU touchdown should not have counted because the ball was recovered at the 2-yard line. The game was decided by seven points. The system is failing players and fans in both leagues. Mahomes added a smiling face emoji to show her sarcasm. A crucial field goal miss by Harrison Butker allowed Denver to enter the game. Two fourth-quarter touchdowns by the Broncos secured the lead for them. Kansas City squandered a double-digit lead during the second half. The penalties and the bad calls are the only reasons this loss happened. Fans want to see the game played fairly. When the refs make a call that ends a game, they need to get it right. The New York Post reported that the Big 12 admitted their error. The NFL needs to admit their error too.

item.title: To dive or not to dive? Football's big dilemma
item.description: Bradley Barcola delivered a cross into the Arsenal penalty area, with Liverpool striker Alexander Isak seemingly ready to nod home an equaliser. The Sweden international just failed to get his head on the ball, and it drifted out of play. Isak simply turned around to make his way back up the field in readiness for the goal-kick. Nothing to see here. Or was there? Replays showed that Jurrien Timber had a handful of Isak's shirt. Surely that prevented the striker from being able to play the ball? Yet Isak did not complain. The video assistant referee (VAR), Stuart Attwell, decided there was not enough in it for a review. "There is a clear grab of the shirt," Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said after the 1-0 defeat by the Gunners at Anfield on Sunday. "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it." When players do dive, they get criticised. Take Alexis Mac Allister, described as "embarrassing" by Jamie Carragher for throwing himself to the ground, claiming he was headbutted by Noni Madueke in the second half. You can understand Iraola's frustrations at not getting the penalty, so why did the VAR not get involved? And do players really have to dive to get decisions? But on the ground is Calvin Bassey, who immediately gets up and appeals to referee Craig Pawson, arms outstretched. The Fulham player wants a spot-kick for a shirt pull by Brian Brobbey. One resulted in a VAR penalty, but the other did not. One player went to ground, but the other did not.
